svg.title: Where autoclave RFID programs really break in hospitals
svg.desc: Five program-level failure points that surface 6 to 18 months after rollout, each with a fix. One, mounting and adhesive shortcuts: glue-on attachment of an autoclave-rated capsule fails at cycle 50 to 200 and is misread as chip failure; fix with a mechanical mount such as a rivet, laser-welded mount or OEM-embedded pocket. Two, on-metal detuning at scale: a tag reads on one instrument but fails stacked in a tray of 20 to 40; fix by specifying on-metal antennas and validating inside fully populated trays. Three, no cycle-count log: nobody knows if a tag is at cycle 200 or 4000; fix by tying counters to the sterile-processing software such as Censis, Mobile Aspects or SPM. Four, mixed-frequency confusion: HF at the sterile-processing reader and UHF elsewhere create drifting inventories; fix by picking one frequency, since ISO/IEC 18000-3 for HF and 18000-63 for UHF are not interchangeable. Five, validation by marketing claim: accepting 500 plus cycles with no independent evidence; fix by requiring a report against your own cycle of 134°C, 3 to 5 minutes, 2.1 to 3.0 bar.
svg.text: Most failures aren't the chip. They're program-level — and they surface 6–18 months after everyone declared victory.

g.text: Glue-on attachment of an otherwise autoclave-rated capsule fails at cycle 50–200 — and gets misread as "chip failure."
Fix: mechanical mount — rivet, laser-welded mount, or OEM-embedded pocket.
Reads fine on one test instrument; fails when stacked in a metal tray of 20–40 instruments.
Fix: specify on-metal antennas; validate inside fully populated trays, not on a benchtop.
Nobody can tell if a tag is at cycle 200 or 4,000, so end-of-life replacement becomes reactive instead of preventive.
Fix: tie tag-cycle counters to the SPD software — Censis, Mobile Aspects, SPM.
HF at the SPD reader station, UHF infrastructure elsewhere — two inventories that quietly drift apart.
Fix: pick one frequency for the sterile workflow — ISO/IEC 18000-3 (HF) and 18000-63 (UHF) aren't interchangeable.
Accepting "500+ cycles" from a datasheet with no independent test-lab evidence behind it.
Fix: require a report against your own cycle — 134°C / 3–5 min / 2.1–3.0 bar saturated steam.

svg.text: Buy the chip for the lab. Budget the program for the ward.
